card.essence: The irritable, oversensitive remedy par excellence. Patient is snappish, intolerant of pain, and driven to frenzy by suffering—especially children during dentition and nervous women. Cross and uncivil, yet aware of their rudeness. Piteous moaning, demands to be carried constantly, rejects what they just asked for. Pains seem unbearable, often with numbness or one cheek red, one pale. Indicated after anger, chagrin, or abuse of coffee and narcotics.
card.thermal: Chilly, yet easily overheated; sensitive to cold air and wind

keynotes.text: Exceedingly irritable; cross, snappish, uncivil—cannot return a civil answer
Child quiet only when carried about constantly; wants things then rejects them when offered
One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold
Pain seems unendurable, drives to despair; patient oversensitive to every pain
Numbness alternates with or attends the pains
Toothache worse from anything warm in mouth; better cold (exception to general heat amelioration)
Green, watery, hot stool like chopped eggs and spinach; smells like rotten eggs; during dentition
Complaints from anger, chagrin, or mortification; convulsions in child after anger in mother
Violent rheumatic pains drive out of bed at night; must walk about
Burning of soles at night; puts feet out of bed

modalities_worse.text: Open air, wind, especially about ears

mentals: Extreme irritability, peevish, snappish—cannot be civil even when trying
Oversensitive, intolerant of being spoken to or interrupted
Whining restlessness; piteous moaning because cannot have what they want
Child wants many things, refuses them when offered; 'too ugly to live'
Impatient, spiteful, quarrelsome; vexed at every trifle
Averse to company, being touched, or spoken to
Driven to frenzy by pain; feels she cannot endure it
physicals: Teething troubles with fever, diarrhea, convulsions
Hot, clammy sweat on forehead and scalp; high fever with one red cheek
Earache with swelling, heat, stitching pain—drives frantic
Toothache worse warm drinks, coffee, at night, during menses/pregnancy
Flatulent colic after anger, with red cheeks and hot sweat
Diarrhea hot, green, watery, slimy, fetid—like chopped eggs and spinach; corroding
Labor pains spasmodic, press upward, tearing down legs; patient intolerant of pain
Nipples inflamed, tender to touch; infant's breasts tender
Convulsions from nursing after anger in mother; from teething
Hoarseness, dry tickling cough, suffocative tightness, worse at night
Rheumatic pains drive out of bed, must walk about
Burning soles at night, uncovers feet
Numb on waking, after pains, or when grasping objects
Sleepy but cannot sleep; anxious, frightened dreams
clinical: Dentition disorders with irritability, fever, diarrhea, convulsions
Colic in infants and children—green stools, cross, only quiet when carried
Neuralgias (especially facial, dental) with unbearable pain and numbness
Acute earache in children—frantic with pain
Labour pains ineffectual, spasmodic, or patient intolerant of normal labour
Post-partum conditions: haemorrhage, after-pains, mastitis with inflamed nipples
Rheumatism driving patient out of bed to walk at night
Ailments from anger, chagrin, mortification (headaches, colic, convulsions)
Abuse or overuse of coffee, narcotics, or opium—oversensitivity results
Insomnia from narcotic abuse or pain

differentials.note: Bell. for cranial/brain symptoms, suddenness, intense heat, delirium; Cham. for abdominal nerves, irritability, colic. Complementary in children's diseases.
Both oversensitive to pain. Coff. more excitable, sleepless from mental activity, joy; Cham. from anger, cross and ugly.
Puls. mild, yielding, weepy, wants company, ameliorated cold air; Cham. irritable, snappish, worse open air/wind, better being carried.
Bry. wants to lie still, worse motion, irritable if disturbed; Cham. must be carried, restless, snappish unprovoked. Child rejects what it asks for in Cham., not Bry.
Cina cross, doesn't want to be touched or carried, grinds teeth, worms; Cham. wants constant carrying, teething troubles, no worm emphasis.
Acon. restless from fear, sudden fright, inflammatory fevers; Cham. from anger, oversensitivity to pain, colic, teething.
Nux irritable, oversensitive, chilly, stimulant abuse; Cham. more for women/children, intolerant of pain, anger-driven, better being carried.
Both ailments from anger/indignation. Staph. suppressed anger, 'too dignified to fight back'; Cham. explosive irritability, snappish outbursts.

cautions: Mental calmness, mild disposition, or constipated bowels contra-indicate Chamomilla
In cases spoiled by opium or morphine in children's complaints; antidotes narcotic abuse
Camomile tea given for colic can provoke convulsions in infants—ironic iatrogenic proving
Not for sluggish, calm, gentle temperaments—only for irritable, oversensitive states
